question.text: PMS management fees paid by client are:

answer.text: NOT deductible under Income Tax Act

explanation.text: The Logic: Under prevailing Indian income-tax practice and well-settled tribunal/case-law positions, PMS management fees paid directly by an individual investor are not allowed as a deduction against the investor's capital-gains income from the PMS portfolio. The fee is paid out of post-tax money rather than reducing the taxable gain. The Trap: 'Deductible as expense' contradicts the settled position; 'deductible up to 1%' invents a cap that does not exist; treating the fee as 'capital expenditure' would imply it can be added to the cost of acquisition of individual securities, which is not how PMS portfolio accounting works. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook (pp. 141, 155-156, 185-190) lists PMS fees and expenses and requires that tax implications / TDS be disclosed to clients, but does not state that PMS management fees are non-deductible under the Income Tax Act in the pages checked. The framing above reflects established tax practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
